morphology_entries.coding_note: Generated by build/generate_group08_entries.py from ICCC-2017.sqlite joined to icdo32.sqlite (build_inventory, group VIII), never transcribed from the REDCap option file or the Diagnostic Pathway document (contract §1). Osteosarcoma, NOS is the code for conventional osteosarcoma in WHO 2020 (WHO Classification of Tumours Editorial Board, Soft Tissue and Bone Tumours, 5th ed., 2020, Table 1, as reproduced with WHO/IARC permission in the ICCR dataset 'Primary tumour in bone - resection', histological tumour type note, pp. 1-2: 'Osteosarcoma 9180/3', with conventional, telangiectatic and small cell osteosarcoma listed beneath it), and the dominant paediatric bone sarcoma. The only Group VIII code registrable on imaging alone: Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, pp. 04-05, gives osteosarcoma basis 2 at C40/C41. Chondrosarcoma shares that Table 3 row and is deliberately not built as imaging-sufficient (design D10). Imaging constellation from Menendez N, et al. Semin Ultrasound CT MRI 2022;43(1):97-114, p. 99. 'Conventional osteosarcoma' in a report is coded here, not to 9186 (design D9); chondroblastic, fibroblastic, telangiectatic and small cell osteosarcoma named as such go to their own ICD-O-3.2 codes (design D8). Diagnostic tests: Histology only, so an imaging-coded case shows histology as outstanding - biopsy is standard before treatment and gives the subtype.

Generated by build/generate_group08_entries.py from ICCC-2017.sqlite joined to icdo32.sqlite (build_inventory, group VIII), never transcribed from the REDCap option file or the Diagnostic Pathway document (contract §1). WHO 2020 Table 1 does not print it separately; ICD-O-3.2 keeps the code live, so a report naming the subtype is coded here as written (design D8).

Generated by build/generate_group08_entries.py from ICCC-2017.sqlite joined to icdo32.sqlite (build_inventory, group VIII), never transcribed from the REDCap option file or the Diagnostic Pathway document (contract §1). Ewing sarcoma. ICD-O-3.2 moved Ewing sarcoma here from 9260/3 (IARC/IACR ICD-O-3.2 'Deleted codes and their terms', 9 October 2020, p. 6: '9260/3 Ewing sarcoma, Ewing tumor - Moved to 9364/3'); WHO 2020 Table 1 'Ewing sarcoma 9364/3'. The REDCap pick that names 'Ewing sarcoma' still carries 9260 (contract §2). Subgroup VIIIc2 is the ICCC-2017 table's own answer for 9364 at C40-C41 (range 65), not a choice made here; VIIIc1 keeps only Askin tumour (design D1, registrar review C6). Immunohistochemistry: strong diffuse membranous CD99 with nuclear NKX2-2; CD99 alone is not specific and is also expressed in acute leukaemias (Kallen ME, Hornick JL. Semin Diagn Pathol 2022;39(1):29-37, pp. 30-31). A FET::ETS fusion is the molecular confirmation (basis 8). code_neutral_molecular is false: a molecular result moves a round cell tumour between 9364/3 and 8803/3 (design D6). Layer 1: viii_morph pick 35 carries the right number under the synonym 'Peripheral neuroectodermal tumor'. Pick 33 offers the preferred term 'Ewing sarcoma' on the RETIRED number 9260, which ICD-O-3.2 now gives to Aneurysmal bone cyst (/0): a clerk who picks 33 records a benign code for a malignant tumour (contract §2; registrar review C1).

decision_trees.tree_label: Malignant bone tumours (C40.0-C41.9; ICCC-3 Group VIII declares behaviour 3 only) - an evidence gate, an imaging route that can code osteosarcoma alone, and a histology matrix router feeding eleven tumour lines, with benign and intermediate tumours recorded as behaviour exclusions

nodes.question: A suspected malignant bone tumour. What is actually in this patient's file?
nodes.hint: Pick the highest tier of evidence genuinely in the file. A radiology report counts as imaging. A pathology report on a biopsy, curettage or resection counts as histology.
nodes.coding_note: Build contract §4. Five routes, the Group 6 rn_document_inventory idiom. Every Group VIII tumour sits at C40-C41, so the router's site capture already holds the topography and this node does not ask it again.

options.label: Referral letter or clinical note only — no imaging report, no cytology, no histology report in the file
X-ray, CT or MRI report — no tissue (cytology or histology) in the file
Histology report from a biopsy, curettage or resection
Fine-needle aspiration or other cytology report only — no histology report
A specimen was taken but the report calls it inadequate, non-diagnostic or uninterpretable
options.coding_note: An inadequate specimen leaves the imaging as the best evidence; the imaging line offers a route back to histology when tissue arrives.

nodes.question: What does the referral letter or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: No imaging or pathology report is in the file. On a note alone the tool can record only an unspecified malignant neoplasm, never a specific bone tumour.
nodes.coding_note: Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, rules 4 and 5, p. 03.

options.label: The note states a malignant bone tumour as the diagnosis (for example osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma or bone cancer)
options.reason: Recorded as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) at basis of diagnosis 1. A diagnosis resting on clinical information alone is registered with the unspecified code; osteosarcoma needs at least an imaging report (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 5 and Table 3). Obtain the imaging or pathology report and code again.

resolution_logic.reason: TdT is the marker of lymphoblastic lymphoma, a Group II tumour that also expresses CD99. Code the case from the Group II tree.
CD45 marks a lymphoid neoplasm. Code the case from the Group II (lymphomas) tree.
PHOX2B marks neuroblastoma, a Group IV tumour. Code the primary from the Group IV tree.
Myogenin marks rhabdomyosarcoma, a Group IX tumour. Code the case from the Group IX tree.
MyoD1 marks rhabdomyosarcoma, a Group IX tumour. Code the case from the Group IX tree.
SS18::SSX defines synovial sarcoma, a Group IX tumour. Code the case from the Group IX tree.
A FET::ETS fusion is specific to Ewing sarcoma. Recorded as Ewing sarcoma (9364/3) at basis of diagnosis 8.

positive: EWSR1 or FUS fusion with a non-ETS partner (NFATC2, PATZ1)
resolution_logic.reason: An EWSR1 or FUS fusion with a non-ETS partner defines a round cell sarcoma classified separately from Ewing sarcoma. Recorded as Small cell sarcoma (8803/3) at basis of diagnosis 8; ICD-O-3.2 has no code of its own.
A CIC rearrangement defines CIC-rearranged sarcoma. Recorded as Small cell sarcoma (8803/3) at basis of diagnosis 8; ICD-O-3.2 has no code of its own.

positive: BCOR::CCNB3 fusion or BCOR internal tandem duplication
resolution_logic.reason: A BCOR fusion or internal tandem duplication defines sarcoma with BCOR genetic alteration. Recorded as Small cell sarcoma (8803/3) at basis of diagnosis 8; ICD-O-3.2 has no code of its own.
ETV4 is highly specific for CIC-rearranged sarcoma. Recorded as Small cell sarcoma (8803/3); ICD-O-3.2 has no code of its own.
Diffuse nuclear BCOR marks sarcoma with BCOR genetic alteration. Recorded as Small cell sarcoma (8803/3); ICD-O-3.2 has no code of its own.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Kallen & Hornick 2022, p. 33: highly sensitive, moderately specific; poorly differentiated synovial sarcoma also expresses BCOR, which the SS18::SSX rule above catches first when tested.

resolution_logic.reason: Strong diffuse membranous CD99 with nuclear NKX2-2 is the Ewing sarcoma immunophenotype. Recorded as Ewing sarcoma (9364/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Kallen & Hornick 2022, p. 31. Placed after every fusion rule: CD99 and NKX2-2 are not exclusive to Ewing sarcoma, and a demonstrated non-ETS fusion overrides them (contract §4).

options.reason: Osteofibrous dysplasia is a benign fibro-osseous lesion. Not a reportable malignancy.

nodes.question: Which odontogenic tumour does the report diagnose?
nodes.coding_note: Soluk-Tekkesin M, Wright JM. Turk Patoloji Derg 2022;38(2):168-184, Table 1, malignant odontogenic tumours, mapped to ICD-O-3.2 by term (design D13).

options.label: Ameloblastic carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Odontogenic tumor, malignant (9270/3), whose ICD-O-3.2 synonyms include Ameloblastic carcinoma.

options.label: Primary intraosseous carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Odontogenic tumor, malignant (9270/3), whose ICD-O-3.2 synonyms include Primary intraosseous carcinoma.

options.label: Sclerosing odontogenic carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Odontogenic tumor, malignant (9270/3). ICD-O-3.2 has no term for sclerosing odontogenic carcinoma; its synonym Odontogenic carcinoma is the nearest.

options.label: Clear cell odontogenic carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Clear cell odontogenic carcinoma (9341/3).

options.label: Ghost cell odontogenic carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Ghost cell odontogenic carcinoma (9302/3).

options.reason: Recorded as Ameloblastic fibrosarcoma (9330/3).

options.reason: Recorded as Ameloblastic odontosarcoma (9290/3), whose ICD-O-3.2 synonyms are these two terms.

options.label: Metastasizing ameloblastoma
options.reason: Recorded as Ameloblastoma, metastasizing (9310/3).
options.coding_note: Design D13, registrar review A6: WHO 2022 places it among the benign tumours; ICD-O-3.2 codes it /3.

options.label: Malignant odontogenic tumour, type not stated

options.label: Ameloblastoma

behaviour_exclusion.reason: Ameloblastoma is a benign tumour, ICD-O-3.2 9310/0. ICCC-3 Group VIII registers malignant (behaviour 3) tumours only, so no Group VIII code is recorded. Whether the registry records it elsewhere is the registrar's decision.

options.label: Another benign odontogenic tumour, or an odontogenic cyst
options.reason: A benign odontogenic tumour or cyst. Not a Group VIII cancer.

nodes.question: Which primary tumour has spread to the bone?
nodes.hint: A metastasis in bone is coded from its primary tumour's group.
nodes.coding_note: Receives Group III's pf_secondary_deposit and un_metastatic_deposit 'bone' referrals only when the bone lesion is itself a deposit. ICCC-2017 range 143 (XIIb) admits 8000-8005 at 809.

options.label: Neuroblastoma
options.reason: Code the primary neuroblastoma from the Group IV tree.

options.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
options.reason: Code the primary rhabdomyosarcoma from the Group IX tree.

options.label: Renal tumour (Wilms tumour, clear cell sarcoma of the kidney)
options.reason: Code the primary renal tumour from the Group VI tree.

options.label: Primary not found, and the tumour type is not stated
options.reason: A metastasis whose primary is not found and whose type is not stated is an unspecified malignancy of unknown primary site, which belongs to ICCC-3 Group XII.
